_: The section « Company and vessel names » of the Screening page, form M4F validated by Arslane on 28/09, lead finding changed on 4 October 2026: the first two populations are the fourth verdict on real company names from the GLEIF register, read line by line from the tool's own output (`gleif.fichier`, refused when its SHA-256 is not `gleif.sha256`); the third is the second thousand-name book of ~/Documents/cascade-screening/releve-entites.json at seal `sceau`. The builder refuses to build if the record on disk no longer carries that seal or the verdict file that hash, recomputes every count and refuses a figure the HTML does not show. The date, the commit and the seal shown come from the record itself. {sur}, {lignes} and the figures of the note are filled from those two sources. No em dash anywhere.
titre:
Nearly half of real spelling variants come back strong.
None of a thousand different companies do.
populations: {sur} real companies, each under two spellings of its name in the GLEIF register: each mark is one pair, lit when the tool finds it.
{sur} pairs of real, different companies that share a distinctive word: a lit mark is a false alert.
{lignes} invented counterparties on no list, screened against the {listes} sources of {jour}: the lit marks are what your officer reads.
note: Measured once, on {date_gleif}, on names the tool had never seen. {manques} of the {sur} spelling variants, about a third ({tiers} %), are missed even at the possible level: a name written very differently can get through. A candidate is a name for your compliance officer to read, never a match established. On an easier set, written by a separate AI agent that never saw the matcher, {ia_trouves} of {ia_sur} true pairs came back strong and {ia_fausses} of {ia_sur_f} neighbors did (28 September 2026, before the tool was recalibrated on real names). The counterparty book was read to set the review budget, so its figure is not blind.
